criteria.criterion: check-brief.sh, given a brief that declares itself plannable and whose journal exists at .loop/state/journals/<stem>.md, exits 1 and names the journal; .loop-brief.md briefs are matched by their journal without that suffix
criteria.evidence: .loop/check-brief.sh lines 46-53 (git diff); verified via .loop/tests/scenarios/43-brief-already-run.sh and manual run of check-brief.sh on docs/briefs/0003-runstat-cli.md

criteria.criterion: A plannable brief with no such journal, and a non-plannable brief, are checked exactly as before (docs/briefs/0005-production-and-insights.md still exits 0)

run.sh, asked to plan from such a brief (including --plan-only, and when state.json holds a plan for a different brief), exits 1 before any session runs and before state.json/plan.md is touched; message names the journal and the override
criteria.evidence: run.sh lines 713-730 (git diff), placed before the branch-cut-from-main reset logic at line 732; scenario 43's second case proves an existing plan for a different brief survives

criteria.criterion: run.sh --replan <brief> plans anyway and is listed in --help; a never-run brief plans normally without it; resuming an existing plan for the same brief is not affected
criteria.evidence: Reproduced directly: fixture with state.json.brief == "docs/briefs/0003-runstat-cli.md" (an in-progress, already-planned run) and its journal already present (which is the normal state once planning has completed, since open_journal() runs right after the plan session, long before any --plan-only check) -- running `.loop/run.sh docs/briefs/0003-runstat-cli.md` to resume that same plan by name is refused with the new 'refusing to plan' die(), exit 1, even though this is a legitimate resume, not a plan. The new check at run.sh:721 only looks at whether BRIEF is set and the journal exists; it runs before the STATE_BRIEF==BRIEF comparison at line 743-751 that would otherwise recognize this as a resume. This is not a corner case -- it is the ordinary way to resume-by-name a run whose plan phase has already committed, which the code's own pre-existing comment at line 749-751 ('Same brief: this is the plan you asked for. Resume it whatever branch it was stamped on') documents as supported. --replan works around it but forcing --replan on a plain resume is wrong and contradicts this criterion outright.

findings: run.sh incorrectly refuses to resume an already-planned run when the brief is named explicitly and its journal exists (which it normally does once planning has committed) -- 'resuming an existing plan for the same brief is not affected' is violated. Repro: plant state.json with .brief == the target brief plus its journal file, then `run.sh <that brief>` (no --plan-only) dies with 'refusing to plan' instead of resuming.

The new scenario 43-brief-already-run.sh never exercises this resume-same-brief path -- every case either uses --plan-only against a fresh/never-planned fixture or a different-brief plan, so the gate is green despite the regression.
notes: Fix is straightforward: move the new refusal check after (or make it conditional on) the STATE_BRIEF != BRIEF / no-state case, so it only fires when this invocation would actually plan (STATE.json absent, or the named brief differs from STATE's), not whenever the journal happens to exist. Everything else in the diff (check-brief.sh, doc/scenario-count updates, --replan flag/help text, run-all.sh's already-run handling) is solid and well-reasoned.
